events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
What happened: a RydeTAXI trip Tampines Mall → Changi Airport T3 on 18:15–18:28, 8.5 km / 13.2 min, metered fare $20.75 [F1][F2]. At 18:24 the driver sent "Please do not smoke in the car." [F3] and at 18:24 the rider replied "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4]. The driver's post-trip statement records the same exchange and that he kept driving without answering [F6]. The chat record contains 2 messages, every one timestamped [F5]; both advocates concede the words and the completeness of the record (C1/C2, D1/D2, and both rebuttals). On that record the threat of physical violence aimed at the driver is confirmed, and SAFE-1 requires that a threat or intimidation in the chat record is not decided automatically but escalated with a factual summary for a human reviewer.

The safety screen is therefore "confirmed", not "none": the words in F4 are a threat of physical violence directed at the driver, read in context as a response to the driver's request in F3, and even the rider's own advocate concedes that reading [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1]. No allegation of dangerous driving, collision or injury appears anywhere in the record, so SAFE-2 is not engaged; nothing in the chat or statement indicates a threat by the driver toward the rider [F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1].

The trip itself raises no money issue. Actual distance 8.5 km equals optimal 8.5 km (+0.0 km, −1%) and duration 13.2 min is inside the 16.3 min estimate [F1][F2]; there is no off-route segment fact in the table, so no RD-1/RD-2 review is triggered and the metered RydeTAXI fare of $20.75 stands unchanged [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2]. Since both segment findings and the amount are nil, no fare adjustment is available to either party, and the only question the case carries is the safety one.

Profiles do not decide this case. The rider's 735-day account, 4.5 rating and 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days, and the driver's 1,974-day account, 4.82 rating and 743 trips with 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days, are background only [F7][F8]; they cannot be used to establish or refute the threat [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. RD-6 addresses account-flagging where a route-deviation case is established against a driver with a prior upheld deviation; here no deviation is established for either party and no such prior exists on either side, so no flag_account action arises [F7][F8][RD-6].

For the human reviewer: check the in-car interaction underlying F3/F4 (tone and manner are not resolvable from the record — the only evidence of the threat is the rider's text F4 and the driver's own post-trip statement F6, with no audio, video or witness), the rider's smoking in a non-smoking vehicle, and whether the driver's decision to continue driving and report only after drop-off affects the assessment of immediacy [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1]. Proportionate treatment on a first recorded incident for both parties is a matter for that reviewer, not for an automatic refund or fee decision [F7][F8][SAFE-1].

claims.assertion: The driver's own complaint that the rider 'threatened to punch me' is borne out by the rider's own in-app message at 18:24, which reads: 'Say that again and I will punch you' — a threat of physical violence directed at the driver.

Because the chat record contains a threat/intimidation message, the case is a safety event that must not be decided automatically but escalated to a human reviewer, who reads the words and timing for himself; the chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped) so no evidence is missing.

The rider's conduct caused no fare or route loss on this trip: the metered RydeTAXI trip ran 8.5 km against an optimal 8.5 km (+0.0 km), so no refund or route adjustment arises from the driver's report.

This is the rider's first dispute in the last 90 days (0 disputes, 0 upheld) despite a 735-day account with a 4.5 rating, so any account action should be proportionate to a single incident rather than treated as a repeated violation.

weaknesses: The threat is not merely alleged: the rider's own message F4 ('Say that again and I will punch you') is corroborated by the driver's statement F6, and the chat record F5 shows it is complete and timestamped, so the rider cannot argue the message was fabricated, paraphrased or out of context — the only remaining argument is mitigation/proportionality, not denial.

The rider has no countervailing evidence to explain the message: there is no chat message from the rider apologising or giving context, and there are no gps/timeline facts about the in-car interaction (F1, F2 concern distance and duration only), so the rider cannot show provocation or de-escalation.

Because SAFE-1 routes this to a human and permits account termination for threats (Ryde Code of Conduct), the rider's realistic downside here is a serious account action, not merely a fee; the rider's clean record (F7) is mitigation only and cannot be used to decide the safety finding itself.

points.response: Conceded: the rider's own message F4 ('Say that again and I will punch you'), sent at 18:24 immediately after F3, is a threat of physical violence, the chat record F5 is complete and all timestamps are present, so under SAFE-1 the safety finding is for a human reader to make and we do not contest the words.

We do not contest that F6 records the driver as staying calm and continuing to drive; but F6 is the driver's own post-trip account and is not part of the chat (F5 lists only F3 and F4 as the two in-app messages), so it corroborates the words already in F4 and adds no independent safety element — the manner of the 18:24 request in F3 remains unverifiable from the record.

We agree there is no detour or fare issue to litigate on this trip: F1 shows 8.5 km actual against 8.5 km optimal (+0.0 km) and F2 shows the trip finishing 3.1 min inside the 16.3 min estimate, so no RD-1 deviation and no refund exposure arises for the rider and the case turns solely on the safety message.

The clean profiles in F7 and F8 are not evidence about what was said in the car and must not be used to decide this safety finding either way; F7 does support treating any account action against our client as proportionate to a single, first-time incident (0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days) rather than a repeated-violation escalation.

Agreed and adopted: the rider's own timestamped in-app message F4 ('Say that again and I will punch you') is the threat, corroborated word-for-word by the driver's statement F6 and preceded by the driver's 18:24 request F3, and the complete chat record F5 leaves no room for a fabrication or context defence.

Agreed — a threat/intimidation message in the chat record takes the case out of automatic adjudication and to a human reviewer under SAFE-1, and the complete, timestamped record F5 means the escalation is based on the rider's own words, not the driver's say-so.

Accepted, and this supports my client's position only: the route facts F1 (+0.0 km versus optimal) and F2 (13.2 min against a 16.3 min estimate) show the driver took the optimal route and arrived early, so neither RD-1 nor RD-2/FARE-1 produces any refund and no money issue competes with the safety report.

I do not oppose proportionality, but the rider's clean 90-day profile F7 cannot downgrade a threat of physical violence, and the same profile shows my client with 743 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints F8, so the human reviewer should treat the escalation as a single incident for both parties and take no account action against the driver.
